record.excerpt: A bullish trade is generated whenever the current short-term SMA is above the current long-term SMA and the previous RSI is below the oversold level and below the current RSI. … We will tweak the following parameters and back-test on the daily values of BTCUSD: … short_len = 200, long_len = 300, rsi_ov = 65, rsi_us = 35, initial_capital = 100000, holding_period = 20 … holding_period = this is the number of periods to hold before liquidating … The results were... surprising.
record.notes: SMA 200/300 trend filter + RSI 35 hook, 20-bar hold, BTC daily 2019-2025; parameter lines were code-formatted on page (backticks dropped), results only in images.

spec.claim_summary: Buy when short-term SMA is above long-term SMA while RSI was oversold and rising, holding for 20 bars.
assumptions: Asset BTCUSD mapped to Binance spot BTCUSDT.
SMAs on close with short_len = 200 and long_len = 300.
RSI length not stated, fixed at conventional 14 without sweep.
Oversold level 35 from rsi_us = 35; rsi_ov = 65 not used for entry.
Exit is time-only hold of 20 bars from holding_period; no other exit stated.
initial_capital = 100000 is position sizing and not part of the rule.
NOT EXPRESSIBLE: claim requires previous-bar RSI below the oversold level but schema has no bar offset, so tested as current-bar RSI < 35 which shifts entry timing by one bar.
NOT EXPRESSIBLE: claim requires previous RSI below current RSI (rising RSI) but schema has no cross-bar indicator comparison, so this rising filter is omitted which widens entries.
